I have identified and fixed the issue where `Model.objects.all().delete()` was generating a subquery `DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM table)`.

### Root Cause
When a query without joins or filters (such as `Model.objects.all()`) is cloned into a `DeleteQuery`, its `alias_map` starts off empty (`{}`). When `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias` evaluated `sum(self.query.alias_refcount[t] > 0 for t in self.query.alias_map) == 1`, it returned `False` because `alias_map` was empty. As a result, the compiler incorrectly treated the single-table deletion as a multi-table query requiring a subquery filter.

### Solution
In [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-ttdenqly/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1412), ensured `self.query.get_initial_alias()` is called prior to counting active tables via `self.query.count_active_tables() == 1`. This guarantees that the base table alias is registered in `alias_map` before checking whether the query spans single or multiple tables.
